title: Multiple testing and the problem of peeking early

videos.script: A five per cent significance level means one false alarm in twenty, when nothing is going on. That is a promise about one look at one number. {{promise}} Look at twenty numbers, and one of them will probably cross the line by chance. Look at the same number every day, and stop the first time it crosses, and you will find a winner far more often than one time in twenty. {{twenty}} Both habits feel like diligence. Checking more segments. Watching the test closely. Both quietly turn the five per cent into something much larger. {{diligence}} In Panela's test, mobile visitors seem to respond strongly to the new checkout. Exactly as the hypothesis said. It is the kind of finding that gets a slide of its own. Corrected for the number of segments examined, it is not significant. {{mobile}} And two thousand simulated tests where nothing changed at all show what daily peeking does: more than a quarter of them declare a winner. {{peek}} This lesson measures both, and gives the rules that keep five per cent meaning five per cent. {{end}}
